title: Per-tenant burst cap reconciliation bug — AcmeHealth production shortfall
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
During a traffic spike on 2026-03-02 morning, AcmeHealth (enterprise Dedicated customer) experienced sustained 429/503 errors for ~18 minutes. The platform failed to satisfy burst capacity despite available cluster headroom; requests were rejected by the per-tenant admission controller.

Scope:
- Affected only Dedicated reserved pools with per-tenant burst overrides enabled.
- Impacted 1 customer (AcmeHealth) across two regions (us-west-2 and eu-west-1) intermittently.

Immediate customer-visible symptoms:
- Elevated request throttles and queue overflows in the per-tenant admission path.
- Console showed reserved pool utilization < 70% while customer traffic was queued/failed.

Why this ticket exists:
This ticket captures the incident timeline, root cause, hotfix deployed, verification steps, long-term remediation items, and customer communications. It also records PRs, tests, and follow-ups for the autoscaler and admission controller code paths.
timeline_comments: 2026-03-02 08:14 UTC — Paging alert: Dedicated:High-429-rate for AcmeHealth. On-call (Ravi) acknowledged.
2026-03-02 08:18 UTC — Initial triage: queue growth observed in admission-controller; cluster workers show spare GPU capacity. Routing and network checks OK.
2026-03-02 08:25 UTC — Mitigation 1: temporarily raise per-tenant burst_limit to +30% for AcmeHealth (manual override) which reduced errors but did not fully eliminate throttles.

2026-03-02 08:40 UTC — Root cause hypothesis: autoscaler reconciliation applies global pool scaling before per-tenant burst allocations are reconciled. Race causes admission controller to see an outdated per-tenant cap until next reconciliation loop.

2026-03-02 08:55 UTC — Hotfix release vdedicated-2026.03.02-hotfix1: change reconciliation ordering to apply per-tenant allocations before global scaling finalization; added locking around allocation state. Deployed to canary then prod for AcmeHealth. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4382
2026-03-02 09:05 UTC — Observed error rate drop to baseline within 4 minutes of hotfix. Customer success engaged and initial incident message sent to AcmeHealth SREs.
2026-03-03 10:30 UTC — Post-hotfix monitoring shows no recurrence for 48 hours. Began deeper code review and stress testing.

2026-03-05 14:00 UTC — Root cause confirmed: a case in the autoscaler reconciliation state machine where per-tenant burst overrides were stored in transient memory map and a subsequent worker restart could revert to stale default cap. The admission controller read the stale cap due to a race between cache refresh and write-back ordering. See investigation notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/dedicated/autoscaler-reconcile-2026

2026-03-09 11:15 UTC — Long-term fixes merged: durable per-tenant allocation persisted to the coordination store (etcd) with epoched writes and a reconciliation id. Added unit + integration tests around worker restart and concurrent updates. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4410

2026-03-10 17:45 UTC — Release: dedicated-2026.03.10 includes the durable allocation persistence and admission-controller cache invalidation on allocation epoch bump. Deployed across all Dedicated regions.

2026-03-12 09:00 UTC — Customer retrospective call with AcmeHealth; follow-up items and SLA credit discussed. Incident marked as resolved. Postmortem being published to internal doc and external incident summary for customer.
root_cause: A race in the autoscaler reconciliation ordering combined with transient in-memory storage of per-tenant burst overrides. In certain sequences (worker restart + concurrent scale decision), the admission controller read a stale cap while pool scaling was in-flight, causing per-tenant requests to be rejected even though overall pool capacity existed.
resolution:
Immediate: manual per-tenant override and emergency reconciliation ordering change (hotfix).
Permanent: persist per-tenant allocations to the coordination store with epoched writes, ensure admission controller invalidates cache on epoch bump, and add reconciliation ordering tests. Deployed in dedicated-2026.03.10.
verification_steps: Added unit tests that simulate concurrent reconcile + worker restart scenarios (infra PR 4410).
End-to-end stress test with synthetic AcmeHealth traffic at 3x baseline using the dedicated test harness in us-west-2.
Monitoring: new alert 'tenant-admission-lag' triggers if admission cache epoch differs from allocation epoch for > 5s.
Runbook updated: autoscaler quick-reconcile command and temporary per-tenant override steps documented in Confluence.
postmortem_actions: P0: Add e2e regression that simulates worker restarts during reconcile — owner: Ravi — ETA 2026-03-20
P1: Extend dedicated autoscaling telemetry to include per-tenant allocation epoch — owner: Observability team — ETA 2026-03-17
P1: Add SLA playbook step for automatic temporary burst bump for enterprise customers during detected reconcile races — owner: SRE/Product — ETA 2026-04-01
P2: UX: expose allocation epoch and last-applied timestamp in Console for debugging — owner: Console team — ETA 2026-05-01
P3: Run protective capacity audits quarterly to validate reserved pools vs. burst profiles — owner: Capacity Planning — recurring
customer_communication: 2026-03-02 09:15 UTC — Outbound incident update to AcmeHealth SREs with mitigation and ETA for full fix.
2026-03-03 15:00 UTC — Follow-up summary with timeline and temporary measures while devs validate fixes.
2026-03-12 13:30 UTC — Post-incident call; agreed SLA credit and a short roadmap of platform changes. Customer satisfied with remediation and monitoring improvements.
